title: Anatomical Reconstructions of the Human Cardiac Venous System using Contrast-computed Tomography of Perfusion-fixed Specimens
protocol: Obtain isolated human hearts fresh and subsequently perfusion fix them in 10% buffered formalin in their end-diastolic state.
Rinse the hearts to be scanned in water the day before scanning to remove the majority of the formalin.
Cannulate the coronary sinus (CS) vein within each heart with a venogram balloon catheter.
Inflate the balloon of this venogram catheter to anchor the catheter in the CS.
Place each heart within a sealable polymer container on top of a sponge designed so that the heart can sit in its anatomical position.
Position a given heart on the CT scanner bed as if a patient was lying supine and head first.
Connect the proximal end of the venogram catheter to an injector containing two injection syringes: one for contrast and one for saline.
Automatically inject 40 ml of contrast into the cardiac venous system at 5 ml/sec.
CT scan the heart 8 sec after initiating the contrast injection.
Set the CT scan to a resolution of 512 x 512 pixels with a slice thickness of 0.6 mm.
Automatically inject 40 ml of saline into the cardiac venous system at 5 ml/sec to flush out the contrast.
Export the CT dicom images onto an external hard drive.
Upload CT dicom images into Mimics Software.
Generate a mask for the CT images that only contains pixels with high Hounsfield units to highlight only the contrast present in the heart.
Remove contrast that has leaked into the chambers or diffused into the tissue so that the mask only contains the contrast within the major cardiac veins.
Manually fill in air pockets within a given vein frame by frame.
Generate a 3D object from the resultant mask.
Smooth and wrap this object to eliminate rough geometries.
Generate centerlines for each created 3D model.
Measure the arc length, branching angle, tortuousity (arc length/linear distance), and diameters for each major vessel in each heart using these centerlines.
